sentences.text: They spent over five billion dollars widening the Panama Canal, and the giant new ships still scrape by with barely any room on either wall.
Back in nineteen fourteen, digging a ditch across the jungle connected two oceans and changed global trade forever.
Over twenty-five thousand worker lives lost to malaria and yellow fever in the brutal tropical mud.
Fast forward a century, and cargo ships got so big they couldn't even fit through the old locks anymore.
So engineers launched a colossal project: brand new, gigantic concrete water elevators to lift floating cities.
Instead of pumps, gravity does all the work, draining lake water to float ships uphill.
The new ships are so wide they leave just a few meters on each side.
There is zero room for bad steering.
Powerful tugboats tie onto both ends to guide the giant beast through safely.
The canal runs on rainwater, so when a drought hits, ships pay millions just to skip the line.
Around forty percent of all US container traffic squeezes through this exact tropical bottleneck.
Instead of sailing all the way around South America, you cut about eight thousand miles off the trip in one afternoon.
Humanity literally cut a continent in half so your TV could arrive faster.
